analysis.title: 1998 Or 2000? Goldman's Delta One Head Bets On LTCM, Not Pets.com, After Nasdaq's Worst Day Since COVID
key_insights: Goldman's head of Delta One trading Rich Privorotsky describes Thursday's move as a violent catch down: Nasdaq -5.5%, SOX -12%, S&P -4.4% (worst day since April 2025). His reasoning: if data center construction slows sharply, nominal growth expectations look unrealistic and the cyclicals that rallied Wednesday are mispriced.

Privorotsky points to leveraged ETF rebalancing with mechanical selling into the close in semis and the NDX, combined with negative dealer gamma, as a self-reinforcing liquidation. VVIX had its largest one-day move since Feb 5, 2018.

GS sales trader Ariana Contessa: VVIX up nearly 45 points, second-largest one-day rise ever. VIX rose 67% to 27.77. The desk's Vol Panic Index hit 9.3 out of 10. Many AI-related baskets had their biggest down day since the launch of ChatGPT.

Nomura's Charlie McElligott estimated $47B of levered ETF selling and $61B of vol-control supply, with dealers about $7B short gamma per 1% S&P move. UBS's desk said risk-control funds could sell likely over $100B on Friday.

Futures closed below the medium-term CTA threshold at 7,549. Contessa expects incremental US supply on top of $7.48B of S&P already for sale over the next week in Goldman's down-2.5-standard-deviation scenario.

GS cash desk net sold $3B on Thursday, $2.2B of it Tech, extending the Tech unwind to -$21B. Privorotsky calls the absence of underlying demand, particularly from long-only funds, the real problem, with multi-strat, quant, long-only and retail all selling in the same direction.
Contessa: ETFs took 32% of the tape, and there was no offsetting bid for Hyperscalers or Defensive Tech, the bid that rescued the index on Wednesday.

Privorotsky leans toward a 1998-style liquidity accident rather than March 2000. His argument: leaders have real revenues, cash flows and balance sheets, and delaying data centers does not destroy compute demand. He names the scale of spending and uncertainty over returns as the uncomfortable parallel with 2000.

Privorotsky splits AI worries into four: financing, revenue to justify investment, power and permitting, and unsustainable aggregate spend. He says the market latched onto power and permitting, arguably the least important.

Hyperscalers have issued $296B of debt this year, above GS's prior full-year forecast of $250B and about 9% of all IG supply across currencies. Data center CDS rose above 500bps on Thursday, a record, and CoreWeave bond spreads topped 1,200bps.

Valuation reset: GS TMT trader Peter Callahan says SOX multiples have compressed about 50% from the June/July highs. Privorotsky's Tuesday math put Nvidia at 10x blended 24-month forward earnings, the lowest since 2013. The article contrasts this with Cisco at well over 100x in 2000.

Goldman estimates state-level moratoria could freeze about 45% of planned US data center capacity, with Texas about a quarter of it. Privorotsky reads Texas Governor-elect Hinojosa's comments as a regulatory reset, not ideological rejection, and thinks actual spending could surprise positively.

GS IR desk says Hinojosa indicated already-permitted data centers can finish construction (per CNBC), likely protecting much of the buildout through 2027 and into 2028. GS economists expect any moratoria to be short-lived.
Heatmap survey cited by Jefferies: share of Americans who strongly oppose a data center near them rose from 24% in September 2025 to 61% in August 2026. The Texas legislative session ends May 31.

Technical levels: Nasdaq has broken its 200-day moving average while the S&P sits just above, which Privorotsky says needs to hold. The NDX is retesting the base trendline from April 2025 and March 2026 (Callahan chart).

Privorotsky thinks the last leg has overextended in higher-quality tech, naming TSMC and ASML. He says the narrative would change on political reflexivity around AI investment, stabilization in funding markets, and evidence that spending and demand remain intact.
Oil rebounded roughly 4% Thursday as markets got ahead of themselves pricing an immediate Iran off-ramp. Privorotsky says it is hard to see the broader tape perform without more confidence on energy.

Overnight Friday: Nikkei -5.8% into a bear market, Kospi -4.6% after a circuit breaker, Stoxx 600 opened down 1.5%. October payrolls at 8:30am ET, GS expects +75K vs +65K consensus, and the S&P straddle prices a 1.45% move, the most since March.

Privorotsky stands by his pre-election view: the S&P has been higher 12 months after every one of the 19 midterms since 1950. He calls it a 12-month observation, not a one-month forecast, and expects playing defense into the weekend.

The author disputes the 1998 analogy: Greenspan cut three times in seven weeks in 1998, while markets now price roughly 65% odds of a December hike and Cleveland Fed's Hammack argued for restrictive policy. The author's view is that 1998 is the right destination but 2000 may be the route for a few more weeks.

sector_views.rationale: SOX fell 12% Thursday and multiples are down about 50% from the June/July highs. Privorotsky sees the de-rating as justified by uncertainties but the last leg as overextended.
Moratoria risk could freeze about 45% of planned capacity, but GS sees a regulatory reset and permitted projects protected through 2027-2028. Financing stress is rising.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Release at 8:30am ET Friday, with the S&P straddle pricing a 1.45% move, the most since March.
Market pricing implies no Fed easing to support the selloff, unlike 1998, which weakens the 1998 analogy.
Marks acute vol stress alongside the second-largest one-day VVIX rise on record.

tension_points.bull_case: Privorotsky leans toward 1998: leaders have real revenues, cash flows and balance sheets, delayed data centers do not destroy compute demand, Nvidia is at 10x forward earnings, and the S&P was higher 12 months after all 19 midterms since 1950.
tension_points.bear_case: The author argues 1998 had a Fed easing and an LTCM-style liquidity response, while 2026 has roughly 65% December hike odds, $296B of hyperscaler debt, record data center CDS, and missing long-only demand.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Privorotsky says demand, utilization and returns need to hold, and Nasdaq's 200-day and the S&P just above it need to hold.

tension_points.bull_case: GS sees a regulatory reset, with already-permitted projects allowed to finish, protecting much of the buildout through 2027 and into 2028, and economists expect any moratoria to be short-lived.
tension_points.bear_case: Opposition is rising (61% strongly oppose a nearby data center), Georgia, Ohio and Michigan are following, and capital is moving to states that make data centers pay their own way.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Texas legislative action before the session ends May 31.

theme_stances.key_argument: Privorotsky leans toward a 1998-style liquidity accident because AI leaders have real revenues, cash flows and balance sheets.
Privorotsky reads Texas's stance as a regulatory reset, and actual spending could surprise positively versus what is now discounted.
theme_stances.evidence: This sounds more like a regulatory reset than ideological rejection.
